correctness.rationale: For A=[[a,c],[c,b]] SPD, the exact coordinate-1 then coordinate-2 residual update is r^+=(-c/b*(r_2−(c/a)r_1),0), with induced Euclidean norm |c|/b*sqrt(1+c²/a²). Normalizing eigenvalues to 1,kappa and u=tan²(rotation angle) yields the displayed rational Phi_kappa(u). Descartes sign analysis of the derivative quartic gives one positive stationary maximum for every kappa>1; boundary Phi(0)=Phi(infinity)=0. Independently used exact SymPy resultant elimination for Phi=1 and dPhi/du=0, reproducing precisely −kappa^6(kappa−1)^20(kappa²+kappa+1)P(kappa), where P=32kappa^6−131kappa^5−144kappa^4−362kappa^3−144kappa²−131kappa+32. Root isolation gives the unique >1 frontier kappa*=5.36076789614546. A=[[5,2],[2,2]] has eigenvalues 1,6 and maps residual (2,−5) to (29/5,0), proving expansion past the boundary. Continuity and uniqueness of tangency establish the iff statement, not numerical sampling alone.

value.rationale: The exact condition-number frontier resolves a classical practical distinction: Gauss–Seidel is objective/energy decreasing on SPD matrices while its Euclidean residual can initially increase. The sharp 2D boundary and exact counterexample diagnose when residual-based stopping monitors need not be sweep-monotone.

scientific_limitations: Real 2x2 SPD only; fixed prescribed forward order, one completed sweep, Euclidean residual and exact arithmetic; no best order, SOR, higher-dimensional or floating-point assertion.
